name: Payment facilitator or relay operator
oneLine: Verifies and settles, pays gas, screens sanctions.
goals: Verify signed payment payloads fast enough that a 402 retry adds milliseconds, not seconds.
Settle on chain reliably, pay the gas, and return a transaction hash the server can log.
Support many schemes and networks (exact, upto, batch-settlement, auth-capture across CAIP-2 networks) behind one /verify and /settle API.
Screen payers and payees against sanctions lists without blocking honest traffic.
Earn a predictable fee per settlement or per unit of volume.
Publish accurate /supported data and revenue feedback so agents and indexers can rely on it.
pains: Research found every tested facilitator broke at least one safety rule, and fixing those rules while keeping latency low is hard.
Clients replay nonces and present expired validBefore windows, and each bad payload still costs a verify.
Gas price spikes make small settlements unprofitable, and batching changes the trust model.
The facilitator is a central party in a protocol that is supposed to be open, so centralization criticism lands here.
Sanctions and AML obligations are unclear for a party that never holds funds but does move them.
Leaderboard farming and manufactured volume route through facilitators and distort their metrics.
decisions: Which schemes, networks and assets to support, and the maximum amount per settlement.
Fee model: free tier, per-transaction, or basis points.
Sanctions screening provider and what to do on a hit.
Whether to offer payment flows beyond authorization (upfront, escrow) and refund paths.
What to publish about settled volume and how to filter farmed activity.
